findings.finding: The fiscal Q3 2027 base dividend was declared on 2026-09-09 at $0.75 ($0.25 a month for Sep, Oct and Nov, last record date 2026-12-03). Tonight's release therefore cannot carry a dividend cut, even though Q1 adjusted NII of $0.47 covered only 62.7% of it. Management put spillover at about $1.50/share in July and said the board weighs 'current and expected earnings levels, portfolio dynamics and our spillover position'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 dividend was also declared ahead of the Q1 print (2026-06-11) and the stock still fell 14.09% on 2026-07-07 on the NAV drop. A pre-declared dividend has not protected this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it has been public for four weeks. What is not priced is that tonight's release has no dividend-cut mechanism. A stock yielding 18.8% at 0.69x NAV is pricing a cut that cannot be announced until about December. If the market believed the dividend was safe through the window, the yield would not be 3-4 points above peers.
findings.independence: Spillover of about $1.75 at 2026-05-31 and about $1.50 by July, from the Q1 call transcript (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-7-saratoga-investment-corp-stock/). Management also said it would assess closing the NII/dividend gap over 4-5 quarters.

findings.finding: SAR redeemed all $105.5M of its 6.00% 2027 notes on 2026-09-18 and replaced them with about $117.8M of 8.00% notes due 2031 ($85M on 2026-08-26, $12.75M on 2026-09-02, $20.08M priced 2026-09-22). On my arithmetic that adds about $3.1M a year of interest, roughly $0.045 per share per quarter of NII drag from Q3, against a $0.47 run-rate and a $0.75 dividend. Q3 will also book the unamortised cost of the redeemed notes. The money refinances an April-2027-dated maturity and part of the Valley facility; it does not fund a ramp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 FY27 management named the 'full period impact of recent capital structure changes' (higher-cost debt) as a driver of NII falling from $0.66 to $0.47, and the stock fell 14.09%. Lucid and Zacks downgraded after that print.
findings.why_not_priced: The issuance is public, but the per-share coverage arithmetic first gets stated on the 2026-10-07 call and in the Q3 run-rate commentary. Aggregator estimates of $0.49-0.55 for Q2 suggest at least some models still carry NII above the Q1 run-rate. If the drag were priced, those estimates would sit at or below $0.47.
findings.independence: Financing question answered: the proceeds refinance, they do not fund growth (use of proceeds: repay the Valley credit facility of $47.5M or redeem the 8.00% 2027 notes of $46M, per the same 424B2). The 8.00% 2031 pricing is confirmed separately (https://finviz.com/news/394897/saratoga-investment-corp-prices-public-offering-of-additional-2008-million-800-notes-due-2031). Partly offset by the rate finding below.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp in September 2026 to a 4.00% upper bound, its first move since December 2025, and futures implied 4.26% by year-end. Base rates were therefore flat over SAR's June-August quarter, so Q2 NII is not hit by the rate cuts management blamed in Q1, and the forward guide gets a tailwind. SAR's assets are mostly floating (81.7% first lien) and its liabilities are mostly fixed-rate notes and SBA debentures. On my estimate +25bp is worth roughly $0.03/share/quarter, partly offsetting the refinancing drag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None available on a rate-tailwind line. The last three prints were all on a falling-rate drag, and the stock fell on two of them (-3.10%, -14.09%) and rose 1.55% on the third.
findings.why_not_priced: The sector has sold off on credit fears rather than rallied on NII: BIZD fell from 13.41 to 12.18 since early August. That suggests the market is not crediting floating-rate BDCs with the hike. If it were, BIZD would not be at its 3-month low after a hike.
findings.independence: Proxy: macro-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed. The same source shows the Morningstar LSTA Leveraged Loan 100 index up from 96.96 (2026-03-17) to 97.52 (2026-09-25).

findings.finding: Q2 NAV marks are likely down modestly rather than flat, though nothing company-level confirms it. In the market: Morningstar LSTA loan index +0.45% in August with secondary prices slipping and software (12% of the index) under AI-disruption pressure; Eagle Point Credit's July CLO-equity NAV estimate down about 3% from June 30. At SAR: about 60-70% of non-control holdings are software-like per the 10-Q schedule; Exigo ($17.1M, rated red in Q1) and Chronus ($19.1M, written down $1.5M in Q1) together are about 9.5% of net assets; equity is 7.2% of the portfolio. Q1 NAV fell 4.9% on $18.3M of core depreciation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NAV is the line this stock trades on: a NAV fall of 4.9% ($24.42 to $23.23) brought -14.09% on 2026-07-07, and -7.94% in May 2025 was also a NAV-down print.
findings.why_not_priced: The price already implies a NAV well below $23.23 (0.69x), so only a decline larger than about 5% would be news. A second large write-down would be news; a flat NAV would surprise to the upside. The evidence does not settle which, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: The CFO, CCO, Treasurer and Secretary Henri Steenkamp is stepping down for health reasons effective 2026-10-31, announced 2026-09-17/18. Internal promotions follow: Christine Ramdihal to CAO/Treasurer as principal financial officer, Rochelle Kracoff to CCO. Steenkamp stays on the Board and as CFO of the SBIC subsidiaries, so tonight's call is likely his last as CFO.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: public for three weeks, during which the stock fell about 7% against BIZD's about 5%. A CFO leaving in the quarter a BDC under-earns its dividend by about a third adds some uncertainty to the dividend-reset decision. The health reason and the Board seat soften it.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: SAR is down about 20% from the week of 2026-08-03 ($20.01 to $15.93 unadjusted, about -16.6% after $0.75 of dividends), against -9.2% for BIZD over the same weeks. It sits at a 52-week low, about 0.69x NAV and an 18.8% yield. Short interest is moderate (4.2%, 4.1 days). The sector backdrop is dividend cuts at peers (FSK about -30%, MFIC -18%) and 'cracks in private credit'. The market is pricing a cut and a further NAV decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 6 of the 7 prior reactions were negative (median |move| 3.1%), including prints made from depressed levels: -4.71% in Oct 2025 and -14.09% in Jul 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so by construction it is priced. It is filed because the de-rating is about twice the sector's, which leaves less room for an in-line print to disappoint. This name's history of selling prints argues against reading anything into that.

findings.finding: No insider bought at 0.69x NAV. The CEO's only Form 4s since the July print (2026-08-18 and 2026-09-09) are code-J transfers of 280 and 290 shares to an employee as compensation, at $0.00. Zero shares were repurchased under the 1.7M-share buyback plan in Mar-May 2026, when the stock was in the $20s. In July the CEO tied buybacks to the stock trading in the 'high 80s to 90s' (of NAV).
findings.why_not_priced: Absence is seldom priced. If management repurchased stock in June-August, the release will show it as NAV-accretive and the sign flips. That is unknown before the release.
findings.independence: Q1 10-Q: no repurchases in the three months to 2026-05-31; plan extended to 2027-01-15 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001377936/000121390026075931/ea0295366-10q_saratoga.htm). The Q3 FY27 loss on extinguishment of the redeemed 6.00% 2027 notes (redeemed 2026-09-18) lands in the November quarter's results, reported January 2027.

baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with. The findings net mildly negative, in line with the -8.4% 20-day run-up and the 52-week low, so they mostly restate what the price already shows; the reaction history (6 of 7 down) is the strongest directional input and keeps p_up below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar: $0.47 / $0.49 / $0.55): every finding kept at or under 1 point; the refinancing finding cut from -1.0 to -0.8.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): asked what the 8% notes buy; the answer is refinancing, not a ramp, so the negative sign stays.
Rule 5 (positioning and drawdown do not file as evidence; macro transmission is a small proxy): the positioning finding cut from +0.5 to +0.2 and the Fed-hike finding from +0.5 to +0.4.
Rule 6 (a finding inside what the company already told the market): the pre-declared dividend finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2.
Rule 1 (reaction function): 6 of 7 prior prints fell, so p_up stays at 45 and abs_move at 5; the scaled number is unchanged at -0.5.
Rule 7: short interest looked up (4.2%, 4.1 days, not crowded); the negatives were not shrunk for a squeeze.
